newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Mark circles wagons as dlr, stg close in.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Mark circles wagons as dlr, stg close in.

text.p: The mark made a last-ditch effort to defend critical chart levels against the dollar, sterling and yen, but technical analysts said the German unit was fighting a losing battle.
The dollar on Wednesday came within 0.3 pfennigs of setting a 71-month high against the mark and chartists said the 1.7686-mark ceiling was destined to crumble.

"That's a pretty critical resistance level and we're having a little difficulty getting through it initially, but we're not getting a lot of selling interest, either," said Pete Grant, analyst at Standard & Poor's MMS International. "
Last seen in February 1994, 1.7686 marks would open room for the dollar to test 1.80 and the next historical high, a 1.8350-marks peak seen in August 1991, chartists said.
Some analysts doubted the magic widely attributed to the current dollar/mark objective, noting the dollar often pulls back after eclipsing major resistance.

"Above that level, you'd almost have to look to sell it rather than buy," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. "The market is clearly overbought and clearly due for a serious pullback."
Sterling/mark will likely test 3.00 soon, analysts said.
But short-term selling could halt sterling/mark before it continues its seemingly inexorable climb to 3.04 and 3.07, technicians said.

"I've been pretty amazed by sterling's ability to recover even from fairly substantial pullbacks, but we haven't had one since early May, so there's certainly potential for a significant, multi-day pullback," Grant said.
Dollar/yen has been forming a triangle, trapped within ranges from June, analysts said. A narrow range between 112.35 and 113.20 sits inside an apparent triangle spanning 110.60 and 115.70.
"I like dollar/yen a little bit higher. It's possible we may see a couple more days of this trading, then a break to the upside," said Solin.

Resistance comes in at Monday's high at 113.45 yen and a bearish trendline from May cutting in at 113.95, analysts said. On the downside, good support is seen just below 112. Further down, a 38 percent Fibonacci retracement of the rally from 79.75 to 127.47 sits at 109.27.
Mark/yen appears to be developing a falling wedge, with near-term gains called sell opportunities. Downside objectives sit at 63.65 and 63.40. ((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
